title: Kernel bundler hyper-heuristic for seqlen/arch-aware runtime picking
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our existing kernel selector picks single kernels per op using static heuristics that underperform on mixed-length traffic and on heterogeneous GPU fleets. This ticket proposes a 'kernel bundler' — a lightweight hyper-heuristic that composes small sets of kernels (bundles) per model & request-pattern using arch fingerprints + observed sequence-length distributions to minimize p50/p95 latency under a cost constraint.

Goal: Build and ship an incremental, online autotuning layer that: (1) profiles microbenchmarks at warm-start, (2) proposes compact kernel bundles indexed by (arch-fingerprint, model-type, seqlen-bucket), (3) integrates with the prefill/decode scheduler to make per-request kernel choices, and (4) exposes metrics and fail-safes for rollout.
proposal:
1) Lightweight startup profiler: run 10–20 microbenchmarks per model on the target device to measure kernels across common seqlen buckets (prefill short/medium/long, decode steps).
2) Feature fingerprint: compute an architecture & environment fingerprint (GPU family, SM count, memory bandwidth estimate, cuda/cuDNN versions) plus static model metadata (layer dims, attention type, kv cache pattern).
3) Bundle search: offline step (and periodic online refinement) enumerates small bundles (1–3 kernels) and evaluates expected latency/cost on historical seqlen histograms using a cost model. Use simulated annealing / greedy local search to keep search time bounded.
4) Runtime advisor: fast lookup table {fingerprint, seqlen_bucket} -> kernel_bundle_id. Integrate into prefill/decode scheduler so each request resolves to the selected bundle before kernel launch.
5) Safety & fallback: fall back to current canonical kernel if observed latency regression > 15% or if bundle fails.
6) Observability: per-bundle metrics (latency, token/sec, failed kernels), and automated drift alerts when traffic seqlen distribution shifts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement startup microprofiler component and fingerprint generator; store results in model runtime metadata. Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement offline bundle search harness; generate initial bundle catalog for 3 target GPU families (A100, H100, RTX6000). Phase 3 (2 weeks): runtime advisor + scheduler integration; wire in decision path for prefill vs decode. Phase 4 (1 week): telemetry, dashboards, and rollout gating. Phase 5 (ongoing): online re-evaluation job that samples traffic nightly and suggests bundle updates.
acceptance_criteria: Startup profiler runs in < 15s for most models and does not exceed allowed warmup CPU/GPU budget
Advisor lookup latency < 200 microseconds for per-request decision
For 3 benchmarked models and mixed seqlen workload, p50 latency improves >= 8% and p95 no worse than -5% relative to baseline canonical kernels
Automated rollback triggers correctly and falls back within 1 minute on regression
Bundle telemetry surfaces in Console (per-model per-bundle dashboard) and includes cost-per-token estimate
test_plan: Unit-tests for profiler harness; integration test that simulates varying seqlen histograms and asserts advisor picks expected bundle; A/B experiment on a dedicated traffic slice (5%) measuring p50/p95 and token-cost; chaos test that forces a kernel failure path to verify fallback. Include synthetic workloads for prefill-heavy and decode-heavy patterns.
rollout_plan: Start with internal runtime beta for infra-backed customers on dedicated capacity: 1) Canary to 1% traffic (2 days) -> 2) 5% (3 days) -> 3) 25% (5 days) -> 4) full rollout. If p95 regression > 10% or error rate > baseline+0.5% at any step, pause and auto-rollback. Notify customers in Dedicated Slack channel for initial waves.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: profiler causes warmup spikes -> Mitigation: run profiler opportunistically during low-load and limit to N concurrent profilers per host
Risk: bundle search overfits on stale seqlen histograms -> Mitigation: weight recent traffic and require minimum sample counts; add nightly replay validation
Risk: added decision latency harms very low-latency tails -> Mitigation: micro-optimized lookup cache and precompute decisions for hot models
Risk: GPU binary incompatibilities across drivers -> Mitigation: include driver/runtime fingerprint and conservative fallbacks
notes: This approach aims to trade a small amount of startup overhead for sustained per-request wins in mixed-seqlen traffic patterns. It intentionally keeps bundles small to limit combinatorial explosion and to simplify validation. The offline search harness will be instrumented to record trial outcomes so we can train a lightweight ML cost predictor later if needed.
